ios.desc:
Are you tired of wasting precious hours scrolling through social media apps? Do you want to break free from the cycle of constant distractions? Barrier is here to help.

Our app acts as a blocker for social media apps, limiting your access and promoting healthier digital habits. With Barrier, you can only open your social media apps if you watch an ad or wait our 30 second load times, creating an incentive to reduce the amount of time you spend scrolling mindlessly.

But Barrier is more than just a blocker. It's a digital wellness assistant, helping you take control of your digital life Don't let social media control your life. Take back control with Barrier!

quotes.story_title: Show HN: Using ads to mitigate my social media addiction (Barrier)

quotes.text:
I am the founder of an app called Barrier - Social Lock (shameless plug: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/barrier-social-lock/id6448244443), designed to help manage and reduce screen time on social media and other addictive apps. Initially created as a personal solution to combat my own social media addiction, the app uses Apple's Screen Time API to regulate usage effectively. Despite having a small user base that finds it beneficial, I've encountered a growth plateau, suggesting a potential challenge in reaching a broader audience in a competitive landscape.

Given this context, I'm reaching out to the Hacker News community for advice and insights: How have you successfully marketed your apps, especially in environments saturated with options? Additionally, does anyone have experience with getting press releases written about their apps or gaining media attention? Any guidance on navigating these aspects would be greatly appreciated.

I'm also open to any feedback on Barrier itself: Are there features that could make it more appealing? Are there any bugs that need urgent attention?

Thank you for any suggestions or insights you can share!

quotes.text:
Hi HN,

I’ve developed an iOS app called Barrier - Social Lock, which is all about managing and reducing screen time on social media and other addictive apps. I built this as a personal crusade against my own social media overuse, using Apple's Screen Time API to keep apps in check. The deal is simple: apps get locked and then re-locked after 10 blissful minutes of use.

Now, when it’s time to unlock an app, there’s a twist: you’re subjected to a 30-second ad. No escape, no alternatives. Why? Because I figured the only thing more annoying than a digital detox is having to watch an ad. It's my sneaky way of adding a bit of a deterrent, and honestly, because everyone loathes ads, it adds a layer of comedic misery to the ordeal.

I'm really keen to get your feedback on Barrier: Are there features you think could make it even better? Any annoying bugs I should squash? I'm all ears for any feedback that can help make Barrier the best buzzkill for app addiction.

Also, I’m curious to hear from other indie devs on your app promotion adventures. How do you get the word out about your iOS apps? What’s worked, what hasn’t?

For anyone game to try Barrier or interested in offering feedback, you can check it out at https://apps.apple.com/us/app/barrier-social-lock/id6448244443. Looking forward to any insightful suggestions!
